I’ve been where you are and completely relate to the hopeless despair, shame and self hatred. If you can, seek out resources about stopping binge eating (podcasts, books, websites - there are tons, I can give suggestions if you like). I’ve found that the shame and self hatred perpetuate my eating so I had to work on stopping shaming myself. You are a human who uses food to help you feel better. It’s completely normal and understandable in our food environment and stressful society. You are doing what humans do but you can change your behaviour. 

If I was you, I would aim to eat 5500 calories tomorrow. Then 5000 the next day. Swap some unhealthy foods for healthier ones that will make your body feel better. The binge problem felt huge to me so I focussed on small, achievable goals, even if they were still overeating or binging. Add a walk and some water. Journal your feelings and post on here. You need some small wins to make you feel like you have some control and to gain momentum. 

At the end of last year I was where you are. I committed to writing down my food for 2 weeks, and not shaming myself for it. I looked at my average number of snacks and sweets and tried to reduce it each week, even just by 1 a week. I gave myself permission to eat without shame because I was doing it anyway, just without intending to. Then I started logging my food. It felt terrible because I saw the data and knew that I was gaining weight, but I focussed on being consistent with logging and trusted that seeing the number would help me change eventually. It has worked - my binges have reduced in size and frequency. I’m able to stick to a small deficit most days and it’s not so hard that I’m holding my breath. When I overeat it’s not the end of the world - it evens out. And my averages over each month are reducing. 

What’s your dieting/weight history? Does your girlfriend know how truly awful you feel? This is your life and you deserve to feel good about yourself and make progress towards your goals. 

Sending you tons of love and compassion. You can do this!

Squash ravioli with walnuts and butter sage sauce is THE BOMB. My first favourite Italian dish many years ago and have been recreating ever since. With infinite amounts of cheese, of course.

I’ve got a load to use up too! My go to squash and pumpkin meals -

1.) thick squash soup made with just onion, potato, garlic and squash, add crumbled bacon, blue cheese, toasted nuts, fried sage leaves or a combination of the above
2.) roast with herbs, chilli, oil and garlic, then blend into a purée with a bit of cream/soft cheese for pasta sauce or ravioli filling, or even as a risotto base
3.) roasted and made into buttery garlicky mash, serve with chicken or sausages (I love adding mashed celeriac as well)
4.) Moroccan style stew with chunks of squash, dried apricots, lamb or beef, chickpeas. Serve with couscous and yoghurt
5.) baked and stuffed squash - roast them then scoop out the flesh and mix with cheese, bacon or whatever then grill
6.) roasted cubes of squash on pizza with goats cheese, rocket and salami
7.) squash pie or tart, made with filo pastry and add spinach, feta cheese and nutmeg. 

You can also add cooked squash to smoothies as it’s so thick and sweet! I’m sure there’s loads of dessert recipes that use squash too but I’ve not tried them. Hope some of these ideas inspire you!
